text:
lee: quick sync: we're picking a default transport for the control-plane APIs used by Console (policies, quota checks, rollout control, telemetry). do we standardize on gRPC/protobuf internally or stick with REST JSON across the stack?

anika: my vote is internal gRPC. typed, easy schema evolution with proto, smaller binary wire, and streaming fits rollout updates.

carlos: +1 on typed contracts, but remember product folks and SREs often hit these endpoints directly during debugging. curlability matters.

priya: could do gRPC internally and expose a thin JSON facade at the gateway for the Console. that keeps strong internal contracts and gives ops a JSON surface.

lee: idea: have proto-first services, then expose a small set of stable REST endpoints at the gateway that translate to gRPC. envoy grpc_json_transcoder seems the obvious choice.

anika: important: tracing & span context must survive the translation. envoy can forward trace headers, but we should also tag spans with op ids so we can correlate console actions -> backend ops.

carlos: quotas are trickier. the console UI wants per-route token/cost breakdowns. if gateway aggregates multiple RPCs into one HTTP call we need to retroactively map costs. proposal: gateway emits an "X-Console-Op-Ids" header listing sub-op ids and estimated token counts, then control-plane writes attribution to billing events.

priya: I prototyped something small: gateway sets header like `x-internal-ops: opA:120,opB:45` and our billing pipeline parses it. works but messy for retries/duplicate suppression. we need idempotency semantics.

devops-bot: infra-bot: Note: rolling canary for grpc-transcode pool 04/01 01:00 UTC. label: canary/gw-transcode.

anika: also watch proto enums -> strings in dashboards. when we change enum numeric values, JSON clients might show different labels. add a compatibility test that asserts stable enum names in API responses.

lee: UX: console team requested an "approx cost impact" preview when editing routing rules. we can estimate from token model server-side; no need to surface raw op id spaghetti to product.

carlos: for debugging, add `GET /_debug/op/{id}` endpoint at gateway that forwards to the corresponding gRPC call and returns pretty JSON + trace id. SREs can use it without crafting grpc calls.

priya: perf note: JSON<->proto transcoding at gateway costs CPU. we should benchmark with typical Console payloads: policy blobs (~20kb), batch rollout lists (~hundreds of ids). I'll run a 1k/s synthetic test.

anika: streaming model: for live rollout status updates, prefer grpc-web or websocket backed by gRPC streaming instead of polling. grpc-web + envoy worked for our in-browser tool before.

lee: action items: 1) priya to run JSON<->proto perf POC and telemetry passthrough test; 2) carlos to draft quota attribution header spec and idempotency guidance; 3) anika to add enum-compat tests to proto CI; 4) i'll write a short RFC (hybrid-internal-grpc-external-json.md) capturing pattern and envoy snippets.

priya: I'll drop POC branch and post results here.

carlos: I'll sketch header format `x-internal-ops: id1=120;id2=45` and include a checksum to detect tampering.

anika: tag me on the RFC. also include fallback: services can opt-out and offer their own REST facade if they need human-facing endpoints.

lee: final: default internal transport = gRPC. exceptions must be documented. thanks everyone.

priya: pinged with branch when ready.
